=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:1597-1599 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: The refusal-marker comment POST ends in `|| true`, so a failed write is swallowed and the invalid-verdict streak never advances.
  WHY: The park threshold is never reached, so the item is retried silently with no close, digest entry or page, which is the loop the PR is meant to end. Severity disagreement: anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 rated it NIT (MAJOR from minimax_minimax-m3 and openai_gpt-6-luna; highest used).
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:1597-1622 | severity=low | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: The "will try again later" refusal comment is posted before the park check, so on the parking run the terminal close verdict follows in the same run.
  WHY: The item receives two contradictory comments, one promising a retry and one saying a person must decide.
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:1605-1622 (with scripts/unblock_actions.py:819-823 and scripts/unblock_ledger.py:854-855) | severity=high | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5]
  PROBLEM: When `NEEDS_HUMAN_DIGEST_ENABLED=false`, the `invalid_verdicts` park becomes a synthetic `close` that closes the issue as not planned or abandons the project.
  WHY: Two refused model answers are a model or validation fault, not an exhausted set of options. minimax_minimax-m3 reviewed this and treated it as specified intent, so it did not report it.
- scripts/unblock_ledger.py:875-901 (also consumed at scripts/unblock_actions.py:805-812) | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: `_strip_comment_delimiters` and `_clean_text` silently strip `<!--` and `-->` from verdict text, including `instructions`, so a line like `<!-- changelog: fixed -->` is altered.
  WHY: The follow-up issue loses required syntax, such as the changelog marker, which can cost another fix-up round.
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:1565-1567 (with scripts/unblock_ledger.py:1050-1053) | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5]
  PROBLEM: A failed `unblock_rejection_snapshot` omits `--rejected-deletions-file`, so `validate` refuses a valid verdict, and that refusal counts toward the park.
  WHY: A flaky artifact read on two consecutive runs can park or close the item.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:1605-1622 (with scripts/unblock_actions.py:819-823 and scripts/unblock_ledger.py:854-855) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: When `NEEDS_HUMAN_DIGEST_ENABLED=false`, the `invalid_verdicts` park is not parked. The synthetic `close` verdict (built at 1614-1616) runs the normal close path instead.
  WHY: Two refused answers in a row close the item, though a refusal is a model or validation fault and not an exhausted set of options. The tests cover only the digest-on path, and the changelog says the behaviour is intended.
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:1597-1599 and 1605-1608 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The park depends on the streak count read from posted refusal markers, and a failed comment POST is swallowed by `|| true`.
  WHY: The streak stays at 0, so no close, digest entry or Telegram page is produced and the item is retried silently. This is no worse than before the PR, but the fix does not cover it.
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh (with scripts/unblock_ledger.py:1050-1053, snapshot call at unblock_judge.sh:1565-1567) | severity=NIT | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: A failed `unblock_rejection_snapshot` omits `--rejected-deletions-file`, so `validate` refuses the verdict, and that refusal is recorded as an `invalid_verdict` marker that counts toward the park.
  WHY: The cause is an infrastructure read failure, so a flaky read on two consecutive runs parks the item, or closes it with the digest off.
- scripts/unblock_ledger.py:875-901 | severity=NIT | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: `_strip_comment_delimiters` and `_clean_text` silently remove `<!--` and `-->` from all verdict text fields, including `instructions`.
  WHY: An implementer that follows the stripped text may write a changelog fragment that does not match the repo check. The impact is small because the implementer still has the issue body.
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:1597-1599 versus 1614-1622 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The judge posts "could not reach a valid verdict this time and will try again later", then posts the terminal `close` verdict comment in the same run.
  WHY: The item gets two contradictory comments.
=== END FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===

  WHY: Two contradictory comments land on the item in one run, and nothing corrects the earlier statement.
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:1599 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The marker POST ends in `|| true` and is the only persistence for the new escalation counter (`invalid_verdict_streak`, scripts/unblock_ledger.py:743-760).
  WHY: If the write fails, the streak never reaches `INVALID_VERDICT_PARK_AFTER=2`. The item is retried silently with no close, digest entry or Telegram page, and no log line records the failure.

  PROBLEM: The refusal comment says "will try again later" before the new threshold logic may immediately terminalize the item.
  WHY: On the second consecutive refusal the judge takes the terminal close path instead of retrying, so the issue history gives contradictory instructions.
- scripts/unblock_ledger.py:887-898 (consumed by scripts/unblock_actions.py:805-812) | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Stripping comment delimiters removes required syntax from instructions copied into a follow-up issue, for example `<!-- changelog: fixed -->` becomes `changelog: fixed`.
  WHY: The changelog assembler then uses its default `added` category instead of `fixed`.
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:1597-1599 (streak evaluation at 1606) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Failure to post the invalid-verdict marker is silently ignored.
  WHY: With the POST failing repeatedly, each run sees a zero streak plus only the current pending refusal, so the threshold is never reached and the item is never parked or paged.
